rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: let us think from White's side, with White to move. Game Andrej004 × Gleb_6_let, Lichess 2020. Black is a knight up.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.e2: The rook on e5 attacks the rook on e8, and only the black queen on c6 defends that rook. The white queen on b7 also attacks the queen on c6.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.p: Find the move that leaves the rook on e8 undefended.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.certo: The white queen captures the queen on c6, the only defender of the rook on e8.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the capture of the queen on c6: it was the only defender of the rook on e8.
The rook captures the rook on e8 with check, but the queen on c6 defends it.
With this move Black recaptures with the queen, and the rooks are simply traded: the game is level.
Back to the position: before capturing the rook on e8, remove the piece that defends it.
The queen captures the pawn on c7, but the rook on e5 is attacked by both black rooks.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook on a5 captures the rook on e5, and Black is far ahead in material.
Back to the position: look for the piece that defends the rook on e8 and capture it first.
The rook captures the rook on a5, but it leaves the e-file and lets the rook on e8 come down.
With this move Black gives check on e1. The rook on b1 captures that rook, but then the queen on c6 captures your queen on b7, and Black is ahead in material.
Back to the position: the target is the rook on e8. First capture the piece that defends it.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not remove the defence of the rook on e8. Look for the capture of the piece that defends it.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the defender of the rook on e8.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.l1: Now Black must recapture, or be a queen down.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.l2: The knight on d4 recaptures the queen, and the queens are traded. The rook on e8 has lost its defender.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.l3: The rook captures the rook on e8 with check. It was left undefended when the black queen left the board.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.l4: The king steps out of check to f7. White has won a whole rook and is now ahead in material.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex1.l5: This is removing the defender: the rook on e8 depended on a single piece. In positions like this, capture the defender first, even in a trade, and the target is left unprotected.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another position from a game, again with White: Game IvanStankovic × PonUnMenhir, Lichess 2021. Black is a bishop up, and White is two pawns up.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.e2: The rook on g3 attacks the rook on g5, which the bishop on e7 defends. The rook on e4 attacks that bishop, which the rook on e8 defends.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.p: Find the move that leaves the rook on g5 undefended.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook captures the bishop on e7, the defender of the rook on g5.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the capture of the bishop on e7, which defended the rook on g5.
The rook captures the rook on g5, but the bishop on e7 defends it.
With this move Black recaptures with the bishop. The rook on e8 now attacks your rook on e4, and Black is still a piece up.
Back to the position: before capturing the rook on g5, capture the piece that defends it.
The rook goes to e6 and attacks the bishop on g6, but it stands in front of the rook on e8, behind the bishop on e7.
With this move the bishop leaves e7 with check on c5, and the rook on e8 now attacks your rook on e6. Black is far ahead in material.
Back to the position: the target is the rook on g5. First capture the piece that defends it.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not remove the defence of the rook on g5. Look for the capture of the defender.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the defender of the rook on g5.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.l1: Now Black must recapture on e7.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook on e8 recaptures on e7, because otherwise Black would lose the bishop and a rook. The rook on g5 is now undefended.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.l3: The rook on g3 captures the rook on g5, which was left undefended. White gave up a rook for the bishop and won another rook.
rot.removingDefender.ideia.ex2.l4: Now each side has a rook and a bishop, and White keeps the two extra pawns. In positions like this, before capturing a defended piece, see who defends it and capture the defender first.
rot.removingDefender.demos.damas.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in a position from the Game Dobry_Ostankinets × UnholyCrusade, Lichess 2021. The black queen on f3 attacks the white queen on c3, the only defender of the rook on e1.
rot.removingDefender.demos.damas.2: The black queen captures the queen on c3. The rook on e1 loses its defender.
rot.removingDefender.demos.damas.3: The knight on e2 recaptures, so that the queens are simply traded. By leaving e2 it opens the e-file, and the black rooks attack the rook on e1.
rot.removingDefender.demos.damas.4: The rook on e5 captures the rook on e1 with check. Black traded queens and won a rook.
rot.removingDefender.demos.damas.5: The white king steps out of check to f2. Here the queen trade removed the defender, and the knight's recapture also opened the file for the rooks.
rot.removingDefender.demos.rei.1: Attack: now with White, in the Game E_Kudashoff × Jazzyjef, Lichess 2021. The white queen on h7 attacks the rook on g8, which the bishop on d5 defends. The rook on d1 also attacks that bishop.
rot.removingDefender.demos.rei.2: The rook captures the bishop on d5, the defender of the rook on g8.
rot.removingDefender.demos.rei.3: The black king recaptures the rook, so as not to be a piece down. But the bishop that defended g8 has already left the board.
rot.removingDefender.demos.rei.4: The queen captures the rook on g8 with check, along the diagonal to the king on d5. White gave up the rook for the bishop and won the rook on g8.
rot.removingDefender.demos.rei.5: The king steps out of check and captures the pawn on c5. This time the king did the recapturing, and even so the rook on g8 was left undefended.
rot.removingDefender.demos.doisDefensore: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in the Game karlknepp × gillyboy6, Lichess 2025. The rook on d1 has two defenders, the bishop on e2 and the rook on d2, and the black queen on h5 attacks that bishop.
The queen captures the bishop on e2, one of the defenders of the rook on d1. It is now attacked by the rook on d2: Black gives up the queen.
The rook on d2 recaptures the queen, but it leaves the d-file. It was defending both the bishop and the rook on d1: this is the overload from the previous lesson.
The rook on d7 captures the rook on d1 with check. Black gave up the queen and won the bishop and a rook.

The white queen blocks the check on e1, and even without the queen Black has a decisive advantage. In positions like this, with two defenders, capture one of them so that the other, by recapturing, lets go of the target.
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.1: Attack: still with White. This is a teaching example, to compare with the first position of the lesson: the rook on e1 attacks the rook on e8, the queen on c6 defends it, and the queen on b5 attacks the queen on c6. Does removing the defender work here?
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.2: The white queen captures the queen on c6, as in the first position.
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.3: The pawn on b7 recaptures, so that the queens are simply traded.
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.4: The rook captures the rook on e8 with check, but the rook on a8 also defended that square.
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.5: The rook on a8 recaptures. White only traded queens and rooks, and the game is level.
rot.removingDefender.demos.excecao.6: In positions like this, count all the defenders of the target before you start. Removing one is not enough when the other keeps defending without moving, like the rook on a8.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.valeAqui.en: Your rook on c2 attacks the knight on d2. Capturing that knight at once looks natural. Does it work here? Play as Black.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.valeAqui.fi: Capturing on d2 at once did not work: the knight had two defenders. The bishop first captured the knight on f3, and the queen, by recapturing, gave up the defence of d2. The pawn on g2 could not recapture: it would leave the g-file and expose the king to check from the queen on g6. So the rook won the knight.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.valeAqui.er: The knight on d2 has two defenders: the queen on e3 recaptures, and you win nothing. First remove one of the defenders.
The rook captures the pawn on b2, but the knight on d2 is still defended twice, and the game is level. Look for a way to remove one of the defenders of d2.
The rook captures the bishop on d6, but the pawn on e5 recaptures, and you give up the rook for a bishop.
The bishop captures the pawn on a2, but the rook on a1 recaptures, and you lose the bishop.
The queen captures the bishop on d6, but the pawn on e5 recaptures, and you lose the queen.
The rook on d8 doubles on the c-file, but the knight on d2 keeps both its defenders, and the game is level. Look for a way to remove one of the defenders of d2.
The rook captures the pawn on b2, but the knight on d2 escapes to e4. It has no defenders: capture it now.
That move gives the knight on d2 time to escape to e4. Capture it now, while it is undefended.
The rook captures the bishop on d6, but it leaves the eighth rank, and the white queen gives check on a8 with mate to follow. Capture the knight on d2, which is undefended.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.cavalo.enun: Black again. The white bishop on c6 attacks your knight on d7, and your queen on d6 attacks that bishop. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.cavalo.fim: The knight on e5 was the only defender of the bishop on c6. You captured it with the knight on d7, which was under attack, and the queen captured the undefended bishop.
The knight on e5 recaptures the queen: the bishop on c6 was defended. First capture the defender.
The knight gets out of the attack, but the bishop on c6 is still defended by the knight on e5, and you win nothing. Look for a way to capture the defender.
The pawn attacks the knight on e5, but it jumps to g6 and attacks your rook on f8. Then the bishop on c6 escapes. Look for a way to capture the defender.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.cavalo.err2: The queen gets away from the pawn on e5, but the bishop on c6 escapes on the next move. Capture the bishop now, while it is undefended.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.colunaB.enu: Now with White. Your rook on b3 is on the b-file, behind the pawn on b7. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.colunaB.fim: The knight on e7 captured the knight on c6, the defender of the rook on b8. The pawn on b7 recaptured and left the b-file, and your rook captured the rook on b8, which was left undefended.
rot.removingDefender.pratica.colunaB.err: The knight captures the bishop on c8, but the rook on f8 recaptures, and the pieces are simply traded. Look for the defender of the rook on b8.
The knight leaves e7, but the rook on b8 is still defended by the knight on c6, and you win nothing.
The bishop captures the pawn on a6, but the knight on c6 captures your knight on e7.
The queen captures the pawn on d6, but the bishop on c5 recaptures it. Capture the rook on b8, which is undefended.
